key_insight: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization (Ranking-PE) changes prompt search from accuracy-based correctness to pairwise ranking, so the optimization target matches AUROC and improves clinical diagnosis ranking in imbalanced multimodal data.
engineering_relevance: For multimodal clinical AI systems, this shows prompt optimization can be made label-imbalance robust without extra model calls by optimizing the metric that actually matters for triage and ranking tasks.
method: Replace per-example correctness with pairwise positive-vs-negative ordering in the scores matrix.
Use the column average of pairwise wins as empirical AUROC via the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney identity.
Apply the swap consistently in Pareto dominance, reflection feedback, and final candidate selection.
evidence_signal: Evaluated across three diseases on MIMIC, where Ranking-PE outperformed the accuracy-based recipe by +5.8 AUROC points on fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B and +16.2 points on MedGemma-4B.
watch_item: The method still depends on a strong medical visual backbone; if the vision encoder is weak, prompt search alone cannot recover performance.
paper_title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
